quotes.Palm Court at The Langham: #15 in Time Out's ranking. The home of high tea. Why we love it: High tea originated at the Langham in 1865, so this is a historic one to tick off your list.

quotes.Warren House Hotel: The garden set-up is what makes afternoon tea at Warren House Hotel in Kingston so special.
quotes.The Wolseley: Nowadays The Wolseley, a grand, European restaurant in Piccadilly, has lost its shine, although out-of-towners who love to pose with phone boxes will probably enjoy it.
quotes.Hyde Café at Royal Lancaster London: The afternoon tea at Royal Lancaster London in Paddington is slow, relaxed, and pleasantly good.
quotes.The Zetter Marylebone: The Zetter is a rustic townhouse hotel in Marylebone serving one of our favourite afternoon tea experiences in London.
quotes.Jean-Georges at The Connaught: The Connaught is a five-star hotel in Mayfair, with an afternoon tea that doesn't take itself too seriously.
quotes.Sanderson London: We were initially sceptical of the Alice In Wonderland-themed Mad Hatter's Afternoon Tea at the Sanderson London in Fitzrovia, but it's actually pretty fun.
quotes.Crystal Moon Lounge at Corinthia London: The excellent afternoon tea at Corinthia London in Westminster is held in a gorgeous chandelier-centred room, the Crystal Moon Lounge, that's absolutely worth booking for a special occasion.
quotes.Mirror Room at Rosewood London: The afternoon tea at the Rosewood in Holborn includes cakes inspired by different artists.
quotes.The Drawing Room at Brown's Hotel: The Drawing Room at Brown's Hotel is an excellent place to get afternoon tea in Mayfair.
quotes.The Diamond Jubilee Tea Salon at Fortnum: The Diamond Jubilee Tea Salon at Fortnum & Mason, along Piccadilly, hosts a classy afternoon tea.
quotes.The Veranda At The Goring: Close to Victoria station, The Goring is an upmarket British hotel that's a good bet for afternoon tea, whether in The Dining Room or The Veranda.
quotes.The Rosebery at Mandarin Oriental Hyde P: The Rosebery at Mandarin Oriental Hyde Park is an elegant room inside one of London's most expensive Knightsbridge hotels, and serves an excellent afternoon tea.
quotes.The Grill Room at Hotel Café Royal: The afternoon tea at The Grill Room at Hotel Café Royal, by Piccadilly Circus, is the most opulent-looking in London.
quotes.Palm Court at The Langham: If you've been around the afternoon tea block, Palm Court at The Langham in Marylebone is the best place to have a relaxed one in London.
quotes.Gallery at The Savoy: Afternoon tea is served in the Gallery room at Strand hotel The Savoy, and it's pretty great.
quotes.The Lanesborough Grill at The Lanesborou: Afternoon tea in Knightsbridge's Lanesborough hotel is a special occasion experience.
quotes.The Promenade at The Dorchester: Afternoon tea at The Dorchester on Park Lane is a seriously fancy affair that's worth it for a special occasion.
quotes.The Palm Court at The Ritz: The Ritz is a five-star hotel that oozes luxury and is just a stone's throw away from Green Park. Their excellent afternoon tea is served in The Palm Court.
quotes.The Foyer & Reading Room at Claridge's: Claridge's is a five-star hotel in the heart of Mayfair that serves one of the very best afternoon teas in London in The Foyer & Reading Room.
